newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed lower on speculative selling. The spot November contract led the losers as some players rolled over their November positions into January before the spot expiry on Friday. It was said this helped narrow the hefty November premium to January to $95 by the close from Tuesday's $122. January closed at $1,387, down from $1,400 while November closed at $1,482, down from $1,522.

Arabica futures in New York ended a choppy session higher, buoyed by a late-session round of fund short covering. December ended up 2.80 cents/lb at 119.15 cents/lb while March rose 1.30 cents/lb to 106.30 cents/lb. The December/March switch widened to 12.85 cents/lb.

Traders said the Europeans continue to outbid American roasters for supplies at least through March which could keep the upward momentum intact. Political unrest in Zaire is being watched, but so far coffee shipments do not seem to be affected. Given current tight nearby supplies, the market is expected to remain firm.

ZAIRE - Coffee traders kept a close eye on the crisis in Zaire following escalated fighting in the eastern part of the country where most of its crop is grown. For the main Zairian crop not due until December, traders said there was no cause for panic yet. However, they said supplies could be threatened if chaos persisted.

According to figures released by the International Coffee Organization in London, Zaire exported 942,000 60-kg bags in 1995/96 (October/September) down from 1.060 million bags exported the previous year.

NORWAY - Norway imported 50,532 bags of coffee in September 1996, 32 per cent less than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 563,600 bags, nearly 17 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 fell sharply by 18 per cent to 662,100 bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/September 1996 were Brazil (119,200 vs 196,400 bags) and Colombia (124,200 vs 97,900 bags).

MALAYSIA - Malaysia imported 245,400 bags of coffee in October/June 1995/96 which compares to 205,000 bags imported the same period in 1994/95. Total imports in crop year 1994/95 reached 278,300 bags, up from 243,200 bags imported the previous year.

Main suppliers of green coffee in October/June 1995/96 remained Indonesia with 135,400 bags, up from 91,400 bags the same period in 1994/95. Moreover, Indonesia exported 21,300 bags of solubles to Malaysia in October/June 1995/96, up from 10,500 bags the same period in 1994/95.
